title: Why Every Big Team Needs a Rulebook | Principles of Management Ep 10
description:
When Ravi steps out of Chai Corner, everyone does things their own way: free chai for friends, sales nobody writes down, and the best shift going to a friend instead of the best worker. In this animated lesson we use Ravi's chai stall to understand Max Weber's bureaucratic management, step by step.

You will meet Max Weber (1864 to 1920), the German sociologist whose big book, Economy and Society, came out after his death. We visit an office in Weber's Germany, define bureaucracy and Weber's ideal type, then follow one leave request through Chai Corner's chain of command: the written form, the rulebook check, Ravi's signature and the record book. We cover the three kinds of authority (traditional, charismatic and rational-legal) and see what division of labour, hierarchy, written rules, impersonality, merit and records look like in a bank, an army, a passport office and a hospital today. We also look at the limits honestly: red tape, a helper who says "not in the rules", and Weber's own warning about an iron cage.

This is Episode 10 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
